newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KPN SPLIT SEEN BOOSTING SHARES.
newsitem.headline: KPN SPLIT SEEN BOOSTING SHARES.

text.p: Separate listings of the telecoms and postal arms of Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN) should unlock the value in both units and boost the value of the group's existing shares, share analysts said on Wednesday .

KPN on Tuesday confirmed market speculation that it was planning separate listings of the two arms, aiming for a split of the group -- which turned over 21.3 billion guilders last year -- in the first half of 1998.
Analysts see the shares, trading at 79.00 guilders on Wednesday afternoon, worth up to 92-95 guilders on a sum-of-the-parts valuation.

"It's something like 67 guilders per share for the telecom part and somewhere between 22 and 25 for post, and we have some leftovers like cable and that should be something like three guilders," said ING Barings analyst Eric de Graaf.
Analysts say applying valuations to the postal side is difficult, as there are no comparable privatised postal services to buy into.

"It think the post business is growing around 15 percent, so you put it on 15 times earnings and that gives you about 31 guilders a share," said Chris McFadden of Merrill Lynch in London, explaining his KPN valuation of 86 guilders a share.

"Cable TV business is worth 3.2 guilders a share, cellular business 12.5 guilders a share, international telecoms 2.5 guilders a share, PTT Nederland 50.5 guilders, giving us an enterprise value of 100, less debt of 14 guilders a share gives us 86," he said.

"There's limited downside, the yield is about 4.50 percent. On very conservative estimates there's about 11 percent upside (from current levels)...with a potential of cash generation, debt paydown and optimised earnings growth. If you've got some (KPN) shares you should hold onto them," said McFadden.

KPN shares, up some 20 percent since the beginning of the year, have lagged a 30 percent rise in the AEX share index of 25 leading Dutch shares and could prove attractive as the AEX rally shows signs of fatigue.

"For those who have watched the share price underperform the Dutch market -- people are finding very little value in the Dutch market at the moment -- this could be one for people who are nervous of the market to switch into. There's potential for people to buy it," said McFadden.
Analysts said there were some risks to any split as the Dutch government mulls the future of its 45 percent KPN stake.

ING Barings' De Graaf said the government could ponder selling some shares to Sweden's Telia and Swiss Telecom, KPN's partners in the European Unisource telecoms joint venture, or float them to investors, thus diluting the price.
"It's probably a chance worth taking, but there are some uncertainties to work out," said De Graaf.
